title: My Greatest Language Challenge: Learning to Drive in Another Language
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: Being completely surrounded by and involved in something, often language.
A command or explanation telling someone what to do.
The special set of words used in a particular subject or activity.
Useful and practical, not just theoretical.
Something that is required or very important.

sentences.en: Imagine learning to drive… joining classes, talking to driving instructors, and taking theory exams in a foreign language.
sentences.zh: 想象一下学开车……在一门外语中加入课程、与驾校教练交流并通过理论考试。

sentences.en: That’s exactly what I just did. Two weeks ago, I passed my Japanese driving test!
sentences.zh: 这正是我刚刚做过的事情。两周前，我通过了日本的驾照考试！

sentences.en: It wasn’t easy. I went from knowing almost nothing about Japanese road signs, traffic rules, or driving terminology to passing both my provisional and main license written tests on the first try.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易。我从几乎不懂日本的道路标志、交通规则或驾驶术语，到一次性通过了临时驾照和正式驾照的笔试。

sentences.en: I also completed over 60 hours of lessons, both online and in a car, all entirely in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我还完成了60多个小时的课程，包括线上网课和实车练习，全部都是用日语进行的。

sentences.en: In this episode, I want to share what this experience taught me about language learning: how you can absorb hundreds of new words, understand complex grammar, and actually use all of it in real life… much faster than I ever thought possible.
sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我想分享这段经历教给我关于语言学习的道理：你是如何吸收几百个新单词、理解复杂的语法，并在现实生活中真正运用这一切的……速度比我以往认为的要快得多。

sentences.en: Moving to a new country comes with a lot of challenges.
sentences.zh: 搬到一个新的国家会伴随着许多挑战。

sentences.en: Everything feels different. The systems, rules and customs are not the same as in your home country.
sentences.zh: 一切感觉都不同了。体制、规则和习俗与你的祖国不尽相同。

sentences.en: One of the biggest adjustments can be learning to drive in a new country.
sentences.zh: 其中最大的适应过程之一，可能就是在新国家学习开车。

sentences.en: Even if you are already an experienced driver, driving in a new place can be difficult.
sentences.zh: 即使你已经是一名经验丰富的司机，在一个陌生的地方开车也可能很困难。

sentences.en: You need to understand the rules and follow the laws, which may be different to your home country.
sentences.zh: 你需要理解规则并遵守法律，这些可能与你的祖国不同。

sentences.en: And also adapt to the way people behave on the road.
sentences.zh: 还要适应人们在路上的行为方式。

sentences.en: For me, it was even more difficult, as I never learned to drive in the UK.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这甚至更加困难，因为我从未在英国学过开车。

sentences.en: I never learned while I was at university, and then basically I’ve lived abroad or in London since I was 21.
sentences.zh: 我上大学时没学过，基本上从21岁起我就一直住在国外或伦敦。

sentences.en: Learning to drive is often a challenge when you take classes in your native language, but when you do all of this in a foreign language, for me Japanese, the challenge becomes even greater.
sentences.zh: 如果在母语中上课，学开车通常也是一个挑战，但当这一切都在一门外语（对我来说是日语）中进行时，挑战就更大了。

sentences.en: Every instruction, every road sign, every rule is written and spoken in a language you are still learning.
sentences.zh: 每一个指令、每一个路标、每一条规则，都是用你仍在学习的语言书写和说出来的。

sentences.en: Simple things like understanding a sign or following a driving instructor’s command requires focus, intense focus.
sentences.zh: 像理解一个标志或听从驾校教练的指令这样简单的事情，都需要集中注意力，高度集中注意力。

sentences.en: Contrast this with learning to drive in your home country, in your native language.
sentences.zh: 这与在你的祖国、用你的母语学开车形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: You already know the terminology, many of the road rules and how driving tests usually work.
sentences.zh: 你已经了解专业术语、许多交通规则以及驾照考试通常是如何运作的。

sentences.en: You can focus on practical skills. In a foreign country and in a foreign language, you are learning both the language and the practical skill of driving at the same time.
sentences.zh: 你可以专注于实用技能。但在一个异国他乡，使用一门外语，你就是在同时学习语言和驾驶这项实用技能。

sentences.en: So for me, learning to drive in Japan meant studying hundreds of new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，在日本学开车意味着学习数百个新单词和短语。

sentences.en: It was a really difficult, but an incredibly rewarding experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一段非常艰难，但却极其有收获的经历。

sentences.en: At the beginning of August, I turned 30.
sentences.zh: 八月初，我迎来了30岁生日。

sentences.en: To celebrate the occasion, I wrote a Thinking in English Bonus Episode on the things I achieved or was proud of doing in my twenties.
sentences.zh: 为了庆祝这个时刻，我写了一期 Thinking in English 的特别节目，盘点我在二十多岁时取得的成就或引以为豪的事情。

sentences.en: One thing that was missing from my list of accomplishments was getting my driving license.
sentences.zh: 我的成就清单上漏掉的一件事就是拿到驾照。

sentences.en: I first took classes over 10 years ago, but ended up moving countries after just four or five classes.
sentences.zh: 我十多年前就上过课，但仅仅上了四五节课后就搬去了别的国家。

sentences.en: So I decided this year on August 1st to sign up to a local driving school and finally get my license.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定在今年8月1日报名当地的驾校，终于把驾照考下来。

sentences.en: When I first started learning, my Japanese driving vocabulary was almost non-existent.
sentences.zh: 刚开始学的时候，我的日语驾驶词汇几乎为零。

sentences.en: I didn’t really know the vocabulary for terms like lanes or mirrors or traffic laws.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道车道、后视镜或交通法规等术语怎么说。

sentences.en: In fact, I didn’t really even know the legal definition of car in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我甚至不知道日语中“汽车”的法律定义是什么。

sentences.en: Yet, in just a few weeks, I went from that beginner level to passing both the provisional and main license written tests on my first try and doing the entire thing in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 然而，仅仅几周时间，我就从那个初学者水平，到一次性通过了临时和正式驾照的笔试，而且整个过程完全用日语完成。

sentences.en: And this was a slightly strange decision because you can actually take your driving test in English in Japan, but I decided not to do that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有点奇怪的决定，因为在日本你实际上可以用英语参加驾照考试，但我决定不这么做。

sentences.en: I wanted to take the tests, all of my classes in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我想用日语参加所有的考试和课程。

sentences.en: The process was intense. I decided to take all of the classes required in just four weeks.
sentences.zh: 这个过程非常紧张。我决定在短短四周内完成所有要求的课程。

sentences.en: I completed 30 hours of online theory lessons, and then 31 hours of in-car training all in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我完成了30小时的线上理论课，然后是31小时的车内实操训练，全部用日语进行。

sentences.en: Every lesson was full of new vocabulary, grammar structures I was not familiar with, and lots of instructions.
sentences.zh: 每一节课都充斥着新的词汇、我不熟悉的语法结构以及大量的指令。

sentences.en: My instructors spoke quickly. They used technical language and they expected me to immediately understand.
sentences.zh: 我的教练语速很快。他们使用专业术语，并期望我能立即听懂。

sentences.en: At first, it felt overwhelming, but almost immediately I realized that immersion was the fastest way to learn.
sentences.zh: 起初，这让人感觉有些招架不住，但几乎立刻，我就意识到沉浸式学习是掌握一门语言最快的方法。

sentences.en: In the car, I had to process instructions in real time.
sentences.zh: 在车里，我必须实时处理指令。

sentences.en: When an instructor said something like, “stop at the intersection”, or “please parallel park”, I was expected to follow instructions immediately, of course.
sentences.zh: 当教练说出诸如“在路口停车”或“请侧方停车”之类的话时，我当然必须立即执行指令。

sentences.en: As these were commands that I had to act on instantly, it helped the language stick in my mind.
sentences.zh: 由于这些是我必须立即做出的反应的指令，这有助于这些语言在大脑中扎根。

sentences.en: The vocabulary was attached to a real life action, something that I could see, something that I could do.
sentences.zh: 词汇与现实生活中的动作联系在了一起，这是我能看到的、我能做到的事。

sentences.en: The written tests were another challenge.
sentences.zh: 笔试是另一个挑战。

sentences.en: I had to pass a 50 question test for my provisional license, and then a 90 question test for my final exam.
sentences.zh: 我必须通过一个50道题的临时驾照测试，然后是最终考试的90道题测试。

sentences.en: Japanese traffic laws, of course, are full of specialized terms and legal phrasing.
sentences.zh: 当然，日本的交通法规充满了专业术语和法律措辞。

sentences.en: I had to learn hundreds of new words in context.
sentences.zh: 我必须在语境中学习数百个新单词。

sentences.en: Understand subtle differences in meaning.
sentences.zh: 理解含义上的微妙差异。

sentences.en: For example, under Japanese law, “slow down” and “reduce your speed “, have slightly different meanings.
sentences.zh: 例如，在日本法律下，“放慢速度”和“降低车速”有略微不同的含义。

sentences.en: And then apply that knowledge to answer questions correctly.
sentences.zh: 然后将这些知识应用起来以正确回答问题。

sentences.en: Also, it felt like the Japanese written test was intentionally trying to use confusing grammar to try and catch people out.
sentences.zh: 此外，感觉日本的笔试是故意用令人困惑的语法来试图难倒考生。

sentences.en: The exam was full of double, sometimes even triple, negative questions.
sentences.zh: 考试中充满了双重否定，有时甚至是三重否定题。

sentences.en: I studied really, really hard to pass the exams, and fortunately I was successful.
sentences.zh: 我非常非常努力地复习以通过考试，幸运的是我成功了。

sentences.en: I passed everything on my first try, which was my goal, and I actually beat many native Japanese speakers in my exam scores, which I was amazed by.
sentences.zh: 我所有考试都是一次通过，这达到了我的目标，而且我的考试分数实际上超过了许多以日语为母语的人，这让我大吃一惊。

sentences.en: As you can probably tell from this episode so far, the most challenging part of learning to drive in Japan for me was not the driving itself, it was the language.
sentences.zh: 正如你从这期节目前面的内容中所听到的那样，对我和在日本学开车最具挑战性的部分不是驾驶本身，而是语言。

sentences.en: I had to learn specialized vocabulary across several different categories.
sentences.zh: 我必须学习多个不同类别的专业词汇。

sentences.en: And then know how to apply all of these new words and new terms in different circumstances.
sentences.zh: 然后知道如何在不同的情况下运用所有这些新单词和新术语。

sentences.en: There was vehicular vocabulary. These are words relating to things to do with vehicles and cars.
sentences.zh: 首先是车辆词汇。这些是与汽车和车辆相关的事物有关的词汇。

sentences.en: Parts of cars like the “clutch”, “accelerators”,” indicators” and “mirrors”.
sentences.zh: 汽车零件，比如“离合器”、“油门”、“转向灯”和“后视镜”。

sentences.en: Terms for the “road”, terms for “lanes”, terms for the “shoulder” at the edge of a road.
sentences.zh: 关于“道路”的术语，“车道”的术语，路边缘“路肩”的术语。

sentences.en: These are terms that you use constantly while driving, so they became part of my driving routine.
sentences.zh: 这些是你开车时经常使用的术语，所以它们成为了我驾驶常规动作的一部分。

sentences.en: Then there is the legal vocabulary. Traffic rules, penalties, the right of way, and other road laws.
sentences.zh: 接下来是法律词汇。交通规则、罚款、路权和其他道路法规。

sentences.en: These were important for both the written tests and also answering my instructor’s questions while driving in the car.
sentences.zh: 这些对于笔试以及在车内驾驶时回答教练的问题都很重要。

sentences.en: There was also a lot of instructional vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 还有很多指令性词汇。

sentences.en: This basically included imperative commands.
sentences.zh: 这基本上包括祈使句命令。

sentences.en: So these are the commands that instructors give in real time.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是教练实时发出的指令。

sentences.en: In English, it would be things like turn, stop, look over your shoulder.
sentences.zh: 在英语中，就是转弯、停车、回头看之类的话。

sentences.en: These are short, fast commands, and they must be done immediately.
sentences.zh: 这些是简短、快速的指令，必须立即执行。

sentences.en: T here were also some interesting “false friends” that I encountered while learning to drive.
sentences.zh: 在学开车时，我还遇到了一些有趣的的“假同源词”（False friends）。

sentences.en: False friends are words that might sound familiar to your native language, but actually have different meanings or uses.
sentences.zh: 假同源词是指那些在你的母语中听起来很熟悉，但实际上含义或用法不同的词。

sentences.en: Japanese driving vocabulary sometimes borrows English words, but not always in the way that I am familiar with.
sentences.zh: 日语的驾驶词汇有时会借用英语单词，但并不总是以我熟悉的方式使用。

sentences.en: Some words use American English rather than British English, and some are English like words that are not really used in Britain or America.
sentences.zh: 有些词使用美式英语而非英式英语，还有一些是类似英语的词汇，在英国或美国并不真正使用。

sentences.en: Instead, they were invented or used in a different way in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们是在日语中被发明出来的，或是以不同的方式使用的。

sentences.en: For example, what we call the “rear view mirror” in English, or at least in the UK, is called “back mirror” in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们在英语中称之为“rear view mirror”（后视镜）的东西，至少在英国是这样，在日语里被称为“back mirror”。

sentences.en: Or the “steering wheel” is commonly called “handle” in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 或者“steering wheel”（方向盘）在日语里通常被称为“handle”（把手/方向盘）。

sentences.en: These are borrowed English terms, but they’re not the terms actually used in English.
sentences.zh: 这些是借用的英语术语，但它们并不是英语中真正使用的词汇。

sentences.en: Grammar was also a really big challenge, especially in the written exams.
sentences.zh: 语法也是一个巨大的挑战，特别是在笔试中。

sentences.en: This is what I struggled with most and what I was most nervous about with taking the exam.
sentences.zh: 这也是我最挣扎、对参加考试感到最紧张的部分。

sentences.en: I have struggled over the past eight years with being able to understand the passive voice in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 过去八年来，我一直在努力理解日语中的被动语态。

sentences.en: But I needed to understand the passive voice as it is always used in safety instructions and written exam questions.
sentences.zh: 但我必须理解被动语态，因为它经常用于安全须知和笔试题目中。

sentences.en: For example, the difference between “overtaking a car “and “being overtaken by a car “.
sentences.zh: 例如，“超过一辆车”和“被一辆车超越”之间的区别。

sentences.en: One is active. “I overtook that car.” One is passive.
sentences.zh: 一个是主动的。“我超过了那辆车。”一个是被动的。

sentences.en: “I was overtaken by the car.” I also needed to understand the polite and formal Japanese used by the instructors.
sentences.zh: “我被那辆车超越了。”我还需理解教练使用的礼貌和正式的日语。

sentences.en: My instructors were not used to teaching non-Japanese people.
sentences.zh: 我的教练们不习惯教非日本人。

sentences.en: So they were using the kind of language they would use with their Japanese students.
sentences.zh: 所以他们使用的是他们平时对日本学生说的那种语言。

sentences.en: Typically polite, relatively formal Japanese.
sentences.zh: 通常是礼貌的、相对正式的日语。

sentences.en: They also used a lot of short imperative commands, which I mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 他们还使用了许多我刚才提到过的简短的祈使指令。

sentences.en: And then the biggest challenge was understanding double negatives in the written exams.
sentences.zh: 然后最大的挑战是理解笔试中的双重否定。

sentences.en: Each of these different things could completely change the meaning of a sentence, so comprehension was essential.
sentences.zh: 每一个不同的细节都可能完全改变一个句子的意思，所以理解能力至关重要。

sentences.en: This was a daunting challenge. When I first went to the driving school to sign up for lessons, they gave me a very short driving vocabulary test, which is given to every student.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人畏惧的挑战。当我第一次去驾校报名上课时，他们给了我一份非常简短的驾驶词汇测试，这是每个学员都要做的。

sentences.en: I think I answered only two or three questions correctly, and I spelled most of the words wrong, and I was very nervous for the final exams.
sentences.zh: 我想我只答对了两三个问题，而且大部分单词都拼错了，我对期末考试感到非常紧张。

sentences.en: But I managed to do everything. In fact, I think I learned more Japanese words and improved my understanding of Japanese grammar more in the month of August than I had done in the previous 12 months.
sentences.zh: 但我设法完成了所有事情。事实上，我认为我在八月份这一个月里学到的日语单词和对日语语法的理解，比过去12个月里学到的还要多。

sentences.en: I realized that with the right conditions, like intensive study, immediate application and immersion, it’s possible to learn hundreds of new words and grammar patterns in just a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，在正确的条件下，比如强化学习、立即应用和沉浸式环境，完全有可能在短短几周内学会数百个新单词和语法句型。

sentences.en: This experience completely changed how I think about learning language.
sentences.zh: 这段经历彻底改变了我对语言学习的看法。

sentences.en: Before this experience, I struggled with studying vocabulary and grammar in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 在这段经历之前，我在学习日语词汇和语法时举步维艰。

sentences.en: My approach has been typical, probably very similar to all of you watching or listening to this episode.
sentences.zh: 我的方法很常规，可能和正在收听或观看这期节目的所有人非常相似。

sentences.en: I memorized word lists, studied grammar rules from a textbook, and practiced writing example sentences.
sentences.zh: 我背诵单词表，从教科书中死记硬背语法规则，并练习写例句。

sentences.en: But often this approach felt slow and disconnected from real use.
sentences.zh: 但这种方法往往让人感觉很慢，且与实际应用脱节。

sentences.en: I could remember words for a short time, but they didn’t stick.
sentences.zh: 我能记住单词很短的一段时间，但它们就是记不牢。

sentences.en: Grammar rules seemed abstract until I actually had to use them.
sentences.zh: 语法规则显得很抽象，直到我真正必须使用它们为止。

sentences.en: Learning to drive completely changed my perspective.
sentences.zh: 学开车彻底改变了我的视角。

sentences.en: The experience showed me that focused and contextual learning is more effective than passive memorization.
sentences.zh: 这段经历向我表明，专注且结合语境的学习比死记硬背更有效。

sentences.en: I wasn’t just reading or repeating words or writing out example sentences.
sentences.zh: 我不只是在阅读、重复单词或写例句。

sentences.en: I was constantly using words in context.
sentences.zh: 我一直在语境中运用词汇。

sentences.en: In situations that demanded accuracy and immediate understanding.
sentences.zh: 在需要准确性和立即理解的情境中。

sentences.en: Every word, phrase, or grammatical structure I learned had a purpose.
sentences.zh: 我学的每一个单词、短语或语法结构都有一个目的。

sentences.en: To drive safely. To follow instructions.
sentences.zh: 为了安全驾驶。为了听从指令。

sentences.en: Or to pass the written and practical tests.
sentences.zh: 或者为了通过笔试和路考。

sentences.en: Misunderstanding a single instruction could have consequences.
sentences.zh: 误解一个简单的指令可能会带来后果。

sentences.en: I could fail an exam or more seriously, I could crash a car.
sentences.zh: 我可能会考试不及格，或者更严重的是，我可能会撞车。

sentences.en: I think it’s fair to say that in this process, language became functional or real for me, not just theoretical.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以公平地说，在这个过程中，语言对我来说变得具有功能性、变得真实了，而不仅仅是理论上的。

sentences.en: I think perhaps the most important insight I gained was how necessity accelerates learning.
sentences.zh: 我想我得到的最大感悟或许是需求如何加速学习。

sentences.en: When your daily life depends on comprehension, when you need to understand a word or phrase, your brain can adapt quickly.
sentences.zh: 当你的日常生活依赖于理解力，当你需要理解一个词或短语时，你的大脑可以迅速适应。

sentences.en: You can notice patterns. You learn vocabulary, and you can recognize the grammar instinctively.
sentences.zh: 你可以注意到规律。你学会了词汇，并且能够本能地识别语法。

sentences.en: This experience also highlighted the difference between general vocabulary and specialized vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 这段经历也突显了通用词汇和专业词汇之间的区别。

sentences.en: Learning hundreds of terms related to cars, traffic, and law in just a few weeks was possible because each word had a practical function.
sentences.zh: 在短短几周内学会数百个与汽车、交通和法律相关的术语是可能的，因为每个词都有实际的功用。

sentences.en: I was constantly hearing, seeing, and using the words in real situations.
sentences.zh: 我不断地在真实情境中听到、看到和使用这些单词。

sentences.en: For example, I would read a word in my textbook.
sentences.zh: 例如，我会在教科书里读到一个单词。

sentences.en: I would then hear that same word in an online theory class or while watching a video.
sentences.zh: 然后我会在网上理论课上或看视频时听到同一个单词。

sentences.en: I would then use that word while talking to my driving instructors.
sentences.zh: 接着我会跟我的驾校教练说话时使用那个词。

sentences.en: And then I would answer a question about that word in a practice written test.
sentences.zh: 然后我会在模拟笔试中回答一个关于那个词的问题。

sentences.en: So, my biggest takeaways from the experience are: First, that intensity is important.
sentences.zh: 所以，我从这次经历中获得的最大收获是：首先，强度很重要。

sentences.en: I averaged over two and a half hours of driving study, practical or theoretical, a day in August.
sentences.zh: 在八月份，我平均每天花两个半小时以上的时间学习驾驶，包括实操或理论。

sentences.en: Second, relevance is also important. You need to focus on vocabulary and grammar that have immediate or practical use.
sentences.zh: 其次，相关性也很重要。你需要专注于那些具有即时或实际用途的词汇和语法。

sentences.en: Third, using a language in real life situations whenever possible is really useful.
sentences.zh: 第三，尽可能在现实生活中使用一门语言真的很有用。

sentences.en: Fourth, language learned in a meaningful situation becomes permanent or at least lasts longer.
sentences.zh: 第四，在有意义的情境中学习的语言会变成永久记忆，或者至少能持续更长时间。

sentences.en: Learning things in context rather than out of context.
sentences.zh: 在语境中而不是脱离语境去学习事物。

sentences.en: And this experience has made me rethink how I approach learning language.
sentences.zh: 这段经历让我重新思考我对待语言学习的方式。

sentences.en: It’s about creating real life context where language is necessary, and then immersing yourself and practicing intensively.
sentences.zh: 关键在于创造语言必不可少的现实生活情境，然后全身心投入并进行高强度练习。

sentences.en: If you really want to learn a language, you don’t just study it, you should live it.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想学一门语言，你不应该只是学习它，你应该去体验它、融入它。

sentences.en: So learning to drive in Japan has taught me lessons that apply to learning any language, especially English.
sentences.zh: 所以在日本学开车教会了我适用于学习任何语言的道理，特别是英语。

sentences.en: So here is what I would recommend for you guys based on my experience.
sentences.zh: 所以根据我的经验，以下是我给你们的建议。

sentences.en: Just like passing the driving test gave me a clear and urgent reason to learn.
sentences.zh: 就像通过驾考给了我一个清晰而紧迫的学习理由一样。

sentences.en: Setting a tangible, a real goal, in English can increase your motivation.
sentences.zh: 在英语中设定一个切实、真实的短期目标可以提高你的动力。

sentences.en: A goal like giving a presentation or writing a report or passing an exam.
sentences.zh: 比如做演讲、写报告或通过考试这样的目标。

sentences.en: When language is necessary, learning happens faster.
sentences.zh: 当语言成为必需品时，学习发生得更快。

sentences.en: Focus on relevant vocabulary. Don’t try to memorize endless lists of random words.
sentences.zh: 专注于相关的词汇。不要试图去背诵无休止的随机单词列表。

sentences.en: Instead, focus on vocabulary that you will or can actually use in context.
sentences.zh: 相反，专注于你将在或能够在语境中实际使用的词汇。

sentences.en: For me, this was driving related words. For you it might be to do with your hobby, a book you are reading, your job, something you’re interested in, a film you are watching.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这些是与驾驶相关的词汇。对你来说，可能是与你的爱好、你正在读的书、你的工作、你感兴趣的事情、你正在看的电影有关的词汇。

sentences.en: Immerse yourself intensively. Constant exposure to language is important.
sentences.zh: 让自己进行高强度沉浸。持续接触语言很重要。

sentences.en: I was surrounded by Japanese instructions, signs, and conversation every day, and I had to respond in Japanese immediately.
sentences.zh: 我每天都被日语指令、标志和对话所包围，而且我必须立即用日语做出回应。

sentences.en: For English learners, this could mean listening to podcasts, reading articles, watching videos, or speaking with native speakers.
sentences.zh: 对于英语学习者来说，这可以意味着听播客、读文章、看视频或与母语者交谈。

sentences.en: The more you interact with English in a meaningful way, the faster English will stick in your mind.
sentences.zh: 你以有意义的方式与英语互动的越多，英语就会越快地烙印在你的脑海中。

sentences.en: Apply language immediately. Don’t wait until you feel ready to use new words or grammar.
sentences.zh: 立即应用语言。不要等到你觉得自己准备好了才去使用新单词或新语法。

sentences.en: Use them in real situations as soon as you learn them.
sentences.zh: 一旦你学了它们，就在真实情境中使用它们。

sentences.en: I had no chance to feel ready with learning vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 我在学习词汇时根本没有机会去“感觉准备好了”。

sentences.en: I just had to use the words, ask for help from my instructors when I didn’t understand and learn from context.
sentences.zh: 我只能直接使用这些词，听不懂时向教练求助，并从语境中学习。

sentences.en: You guys can do this by joining my conversation clubs and just using new words and learning how to use them in context.
sentences.zh: 你们可以通过加入我的对话俱乐部，并在语境中实际使用新单词、学习如何使用它们来做到这一点。

sentences.en: My method for passing the written exams was to answer as many practice questions as possible.
sentences.zh: 我通过笔试的方法是尽可能多地做模拟题。

sentences.en: I answered probably over 1000 different questions.
sentences.zh: 我大概做了1000多道不同的题目。

sentences.en: Every time I made a mistake, I would make a note of why I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 每次我犯错，我都会记下我为什么错了。

sentences.en: Was it a language issue? Did I not understand the grammar?
sentences.zh: 这是一个语言问题吗？是我没理解语法吗？

sentences.en: Or was it a knowledge issue? Was it something specific in the law I got wrong?
sentences.zh: 还是一个知识问题？是我搞错了法律中的某些具体规定吗？

sentences.en: And then I made sure to not repeat that mistake again.
sentences.zh: 然后我确保自己不会再次犯同样的错误。

sentences.en: The more I saw different grammar forms, the more I noticed them.
sentences.zh: 我见过的语法形式越多，我就越能注意到它们。

sentences.en: I noticed how they are used. I noticed why something might be wrong or why something might be correct.
sentences.zh: 我注意到它们是如何被使用的。我注意到为什么某个东西可能是错的，或者为什么某个东西可能是对的。

sentences.en: Vocabulary alone isn’t always enough. Understanding how grammar works in real contexts.
sentences.zh: 光有词汇并不总是足够。理解语法如何在真实语境中运作。

sentences.en: Like the passive voice or the imperative or conditionals, makes language functional.
sentences.zh: 比如被动语态、祈使句或条件句，能使语言发挥实际功能。

sentences.en: It makes it real. Grammar becomes meaningful when you see it applied in real life situations.
sentences.zh: 这会让它变得真实。当你看到语法被应用到现实生活的情境中时，它就变得有意义了。

sentences.en: So, in short learning a language becomes faster and more effective when you set a goal.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，当你设定一个目标时，学习一门语言会变得更快、更有效。

sentences.en: Immerse yourself. Focus on relevance. Use language actively.
sentences.zh: 让自己沉浸其中。关注相关性。积极使用语言。

sentences.en: Learn from your mistakes. And you see grammar in action.
sentences.zh: 从错误中学习。并看到语法在实际中运用。

sentences.en: My experience learning to drive in Japanese proved that this approach works and I think it can work for English learners too.​
sentences.zh: 我学习日语开车的经历证明了这种方法是行之有效的，我认为它对英语学习者同样有效。​

sentences.en: Learning to drive in Japan for me was probably a bigger language challenge than a practical skill challenge.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，在日本学开车可能比实际技能挑战更大的是语言挑战。

sentences.en: It showed me that it’s possible to learn hundreds of new words and grammar points in just a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 它向我展示了在短短几周内学会数百个新单词和语法点是完全可能的。

sentences.en: The big lesson for any language learner is this, create situations where you have to use the language and you have to immerse yourself fully.
sentences.zh: 对于任何语言学习者来说，最大的教训就是：创造不得不使用该语言并完全沉浸其中的情境。

sentences.en: When you do that, progress can happen faster than you ever imagined.
sentences.zh: 当你做到这一点时，你的进步速度会比你想象的还要快。

sentences.en: I went from no vocabulary of driving, no ability to pass a Japanese driving test, and then four weeks later I passed first time.
sentences.zh: 我从零驾驶词汇、无法通过日本驾考，到四周后一次性通过考试。

sentences.en: What do you think? Have you ever learned a new skill in English?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？你曾经用英语学过什么新技能吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever tried to learn something in a foreign language?
sentences.zh: 你曾尝试过用外语学习什么东西吗？
